answer: Each AI agent registers on a distributed ledger that logs a cryptographic proof of a physical commitment, such as staking a unique walnut token to a designated mesa node. When an agent sends a signal to join a market, the ledger checks that the token’s ownership chain matches a single vault and that the signal’s timing pattern matches the node’s historic heartbeat, binding duplicate identities to the same stake. An attacker must obtain multiple walnut tokens and copy the exact timing signatures, raising cost linearly with each fake identity.
